name: EASA Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0: the Agency's AI in aviation page
title: EASA Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0: the Agency's AI in aviation page
answer: This is EASA's web page introducing the Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0, the European Union Aviation Safety Agency's plan for AI in aviation. It is a short landing page rather than the roadmap itself. Its most useful statement is that the roadmap sets out a human-centric vision for the safety and ethical considerations of AI in aviation, provides an action plan for the EASA AI Programme, and sets the pace for conceptual guidance and anticipated rulemaking. It also says the document is living and will be amended once a year.

sections.body: It is a page published by EASA, the European Union Aviation Safety Agency, which the page describes as the European Union Authority for aviation safety. The page introduces the EASA Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0, a document setting out the Agency's vision for the safety and ethical considerations of AI in aviation. No publication or revision date is stated on the page. The page describes the roadmap as a living document that will be amended once a year.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page states that the EASA Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0 outlines the Agency's vision for the safety and ethical considerations of AI in aviation, presented as a human-centric approach. It says the roadmap provides a comprehensive action plan for the EASA AI Programme and sets the pace for conceptual guidance deliverables and anticipated rulemaking activities. It also says the roadmap serves as a basis for discussions with all of the Agency's stakeholders. On the document's status, the page says it is a living document, to be amended once a year and augmented, deepened and improved through exchanges of views and through practical work on AI development, in which the Agency says it is already engaged. Beyond these statements the page gives no detail on specific rules, timelines, certification criteria or technical requirements, so the substance of the roadmap itself is not reproduced here.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives no figures beyond the version number 2.0 and the statement that the roadmap will be amended once a year. It claims the roadmap is a comprehensive action plan for the EASA AI Programme, that it sets the pace for conceptual guidance deliverables and anticipated rulemaking activities, and that it is a basis for discussions with all of the Agency's stakeholders. No dates, thresholds, definitions or certification criteria appear in the text.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in transportation would use this page as a pointer to EASA's stated position on AI in aviation, because the roadmap is described as the Agency's plan for conceptual guidance and anticipated rulemaking. It confirms that EASA frames the subject around safety, ethics and a human-centric approach, and that rulemaking activity is expected. It does not itself supply the rules, so it is a signpost to the regulatory record rather than the record itself.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Transportation

sections.body: This is a short institutional introduction, not the roadmap. It carries no date, no technical content, no certification criteria and no detail on automated risk management or eVTOL. It covers EASA only and says nothing about the FAA. The tone is promotional, and the substantive document would need to be read separately.
